title: 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3, and binary is why
body: One tenth has no finite binary expansion, just as 1/3 has none in decimal, so floats store the nearest representable value instead. Adding the approximations of 0.1 and 0.2 lands one rounding step away from the approximation of 0.3. Money therefore travels as integer cents in careful systems.
source_hint: IEEE 754; Goldberg, 'What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point'
